THE CUBE, TURNED IN THE HAND

THE TWENTY-SEVEN AS THE PARTS OF ONE CUBE · DRAG TO TURN · LAID DOWN, IT TURNS ITSELF
THE WAYFINDER THE MAP ROOM THE RING THE RESONANCE THE INSTRUMENT THE LANGUAGE THE ASTROLABE THE ROSETTE THE SPECTRUM THE WORKSHOP
A trit pins its axis or leaves it free. Pin all three and you have named a corner; pin two, an edge; pin one, a face; pin none and you hold the body itself, the Seed, the one part no turning can ever show. Every glyph sits at the barycentre of its part, and every line is one clock stepping between still and moving.

THE OBJECT, READ

THE ANATOMYOne body, six faces, twelve edges, eight corners: twenty-seven parts, and the census is the turning toy's own, core, centres, edges, corners, the sticker count the restlessness. The Seed is the core: the one part that cannot be shown, the null never lit. The button performs the reading: each face cell raises its pane of the cube's skin, each edge cell becomes the strut its name says it is, the corners are the corners, and every glyph stands at the exact barycentre of the part that grows around it.
THE BONESFifty-four lines, the cube's own incidence: each edge lies in two faces, each corner closes three edges, each face rests on the body. A one-step move of the standing cell walks exactly one bone.
THE TURNEvery mode turns about its own axis. A named bearing rolls about its line of sight, and the corner's roll is the cube's own threefold turn, the three clocks cycling seat to seat; the shadow spins in its plane; the rosette spins about its own normal, a plate turning at any tilt; the water streams. The hand takes any of them and they yield; laid down, they resume. Under a reduced-motion request nothing turns itself: the stillness is the reader's own law, honoured.
THE SHADOWFlattens depth at the current bearing: the cast shadow of the moment. The count above tells each view's honesty: a face leaves nine seats, an edge fifteen, the corner nineteen, and the corner's blind spot is the Scar and the Return behind the Seed, the triple eclipse.
THE ROSETTEThe object itself, in the round. Sort the parts by restlessness and each shell is already a perfect figure on its own sphere, nothing moved to make it so: the six faces an octahedron, the twelve edges a cuboctahedron, the eight corners the cube itself. The dress trades the lattice's bones for each shell's own frame, nearest neighbours on each sphere, wakes the three spheres as cages of great circles, and lays every dyad through the still centre. The flat rosette was only ever this object's shadow.
THE PLATEThe flat pose, anchored in space and not on the glass. The bloom slides every glyph along its own sphere to the seat the astrolabe's plate holds for it, longitude kept, latitude poured out, no distance to the centre ever changing, and the plate furnishes itself as it opens: the rings the equators of the spheres on the diagonal's plane, the diameters chords through the still centre. Turn it and see the whole plate close edge-on to a line of glyphs, tilt it back to full face. All twenty-seven seats return.
THE GLYPHS IN THE ROUNDEach card's knot is the true strand it always was: wound p against q on its own golden torus exactly as the flat faces wind it, in its own metal, links weaving their counter's. A card and its answer are mirror windings facing each other across the centre, and every crossing is sorted honestly in depth, this page's ink and no other's.
THE WATERThe knots' native sea, one dimension up. Every torus knot lies without distortion on a flat torus in the three-sphere, and the shells become three nested tori around the Seed's core circle, the unknot at the heart of the weave: in the water nothing hides behind anything, and the exiles need no fiat. The stream is the sphere's double rotation, the Hopf's own one-and-one until a touch tunes it to a card's winding, and then that strand pours along its own body, a knot flowing through itself. What swells has neared the eye's far pole: the swelling is the fourth dimension, honestly projected.
THE MEETINGTouch a strand and the stream tunes to it; touch a second and the two are laid on the one shared torus, the middle water, the rest of the sea dimming to a ghost. Their windings cross exactly the determinant of their two laws, and every crossing is marked where it truly falls, riding the same stream. The deck holds no parallel pair, so no meeting is ever empty; the widest is the Scar against the Return, one hundred and eighty-two crossings. A touch of open water releases.
